source.title: Problem Framing and Solution Architecture Course Notes
source.source_text:
Problems and Exercises for CSC10014

Exercise 1: Define a problem frame in system requirements.

Exercise 2: Explain why a solution ladder has distinct automation rungs.

Exercise 3: Compute the cost of 4 rungs at 5 hours each.
Answer: 20

Exercise 4: Compare a use case with a user story.

Exercise 5: Prove that the lowest sufficient rung is unique.

Exercise 6: Write a program that prints every rung.

Exercise 7: Which rung is the most automated?
A. Manual
B. Fully Autonomous Agent
Answer: B

Exercise 8: Describe an actor in a use case model.

Exercise 9: Design a ladder for a login feature.

Exercise 10: Justify skipping a rung in low-risk scenarios.

Exercise 11: Calculate the expected latency across 3 sequential pipeline stages.
Answer: 150

Exercise 12: Distinguish between white-box and black-box red-teaming in LLM evaluation.

prompt: Define a problem frame in system requirements.

source.title: Database Systems Design: The Relational Model & SQL
source.source_text:
Problems and Exercises for CS102

Exercise 1: Define a foreign key constraint in relational databases.

Exercise 2: Explain the difference between relation schema and relation state.

Exercise 3: Compute the maximum number of tuples in the Cartesian product of two relations with 5 and 6 tuples.
Answer: 30

Exercise 4: Compare third normal form (3NF) and Boyce-Codd normal form (BCNF).

Exercise 5: Prove that every binary relation is in BCNF.

Exercise 6: Write a program that validates functional dependencies.

Exercise 7: Which normal form prohibits transitive dependencies?
A. 1NF
B. 2NF
C. 3NF
Answer: C

Exercise 8: Describe the structure of a B+ tree internal node.

Exercise 9: Design a relational schema for a multi-tenant university catalog.

Exercise 10: Assess the trade-offs between two-phase locking and timestamp ordering in transaction concurrency.

Exercise 11: Calculate the block access cost of a nested-loop join with 10 outer blocks and 20 inner blocks.
Answer: 210

Exercise 12: Analyze the execution plan of a query with a clustered vs non-clustered index scan.

prompt: Define a foreign key constraint in relational databases.

source.title: Introduction to Algorithms and Data Structures (MIT OCW 6.006 / ODS)
source.source_text:
Problems and Exercises for CS201

Exercise 1: Define asymptotic upper bound O(g(n)) formally.

Exercise 2: Explain why worst-case time complexity is preferred over average-case in critical systems.

Exercise 3: Compute the value of T(8) given recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n with T(1) = 1.
Answer: 32

Exercise 4: Compare AVL tree balancing with red-black tree balancing invariants.

Exercise 5: Prove that the height of an AVL tree with n nodes is O(log n).

Exercise 6: Write a program that performs a left rotation on an AVL tree node.

Exercise 7: Which data structure provides O(1) worst-case lookup?
A. Linked List
B. Hash Table
C. Binary Search Tree
Answer: B

Exercise 8: Describe the swim and sink operations in a binary max-heap.

Exercise 9: Devise an algorithm to detect cycles in a directed graph using topological sort.

Exercise 10: Justify why breadth-first search finds the shortest path in an unweighted graph.

Exercise 11: Calculate the number of edges in a complete undirected graph with 6 vertices.
Answer: 15

Exercise 12: Contrast Dijkstra algorithm with Bellman-Ford on graphs with negative edge weights.

source.title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces (OSTEP) Course Guide
source.source_text:
Problems and Exercises for CS202

Exercise 1: Define a process control block and list three fields it stores.

Exercise 2: Explain what occurs during a hardware context switch between two user processes.

Exercise 3: Compute the turnaround time of a process arriving at time 2 and finishing at time 11.
Answer: 9

Exercise 4: Compare preemptive Shortest Remaining Time First with non-preemptive Shortest Job First.

Exercise 5: Prove that the four Coffman conditions are necessary for deadlock to occur.

Exercise 6: Write a program that initializes a POSIX counting semaphore.

Exercise 7: Which scheduling algorithm avoids starvation completely?
A. FCFS
B. Priority Scheduling
C. Round Robin
Answer: C

Exercise 8: Describe the role of the translation lookaside buffer in virtual memory.

Exercise 9: Design a lock-free bounded queue using atomic compare-and-swap primitives.

Exercise 10: Evaluate the performance trade-offs between inverted page tables and multi-level page tables.

Exercise 11: Calculate the effective memory access time with 80% TLB hit ratio, 10ns TLB access, and 100ns memory access.
Answer: 130

Exercise 12: Distinguish between hard links and soft symbolic links in Unix file systems.

prompt: Define a process control block and list three fields it stores.

source.source_text:
Problems and Exercises for CS203

Exercise 1: Define the encapsulation process across the five-layer Internet model.

Exercise 2: Explain the distinction between network routing and packet forwarding.

Exercise 3: Compute the transmission delay for a 1500-byte packet over a 10 Mbps link in milliseconds.
Answer: 1.2

Exercise 4: Compare TCP Reno slow start and congestion avoidance mechanisms.

Exercise 5: Prove that the alternating-bit protocol guarantees reliable delivery across a lossy channel.

Exercise 6: Write a program that computes the IPv4 broadcast address from a CIDR prefix.

Exercise 7: Which protocol operates at the transport layer?
A. IP
B. TCP
C. BGP
